requires.description: Ids of text or multiple-choice fields that must be filled in before this button can be pressed.

url.description: A link: the page it opens

actions.description: Up to 4. A button { id, label, style?, requires? } is an answer: the event then waits for someone to press one. A link { label, url } only opens a page.

callbackUrl.description: Where EmitKit POSTs the answer (event.answered) or the expiry (event.expired), signed with the project's callback secret (Standard Webhooks). https only.

channelName.description: Channel name. The Channel is created automatically when it does not exist.

expiresIn.description: Seconds an event with buttons or fields waits for an answer: 10 to 604800, default 86400 (24 hours). After that, answer.status is expired.

default.description: An option id (an array of ids when multiple). A single choice without one starts on its first option.

multiple.description: Let the person pick several options (checkboxes).

unit.description: Shown next to the value, e.g. $ or %

fields.description: Up to 5 inputs the person fills in: a choice (one or several options), text, a number or a yes/no. The answer reports them in answer.values by field id. Fields without buttons get a Send button.

notify.description: Send a web push notification to devices subscribed to the Channel.

resume.description: Your own state, sent back as is in the callback and GET /v1/events/{id}, so a serverless handler can carry on without a database. Never shown to people.

CreateEventRequest.description: An event. Add actions with an id (buttons) and/or fields to ask a person something: the event then waits for an answer, returned in data.answer by this call and by GET /v1/events/{id}. Actions with a url are links and never wait. Objects inside fields and actions reject settings that don't exist. Rules the schema can't express: field and button ids are unique; submit is reserved for the Send button; requires names text or multiple-choice fields; a choice default names its options; expiresIn, callbackUrl and resume only on an event that waits; callbackUrl is https and never EmitKit itself; an event that waits can't set notify to false.

Answer.description: The answer to an event that waits: pending until someone presses a button, then answered; expired after expiresAt; canceled by the sender. First answer wins. action, values, by and at are null until it's answered.

action.description: The id of the pressed button (submit when fields had no buttons).

expiresAt.description: When a pending event stops waiting.

url.description: The answer page (needs a signed-in member). Pushes for this event open it.

values.description: Field values by field id: an option id (an array for multiple), text, a number or a boolean. Empty text fields are left out.

Event.description: An event, as createEvent, getEvent and cancelEvent return it: the event with its fields, actions (both [] when none) and answer (null when it doesn't wait). Events are kept for 90 days; after that getEvent returns 404.

id.description: A button: what the answer reports, e.g. approve

requires.description: Field ids that must be filled in before this button can be pressed.

url.description: A link: the page it opens

actions.description: The event's buttons and links ([] when none).

answer.description: null when the event doesn't wait for an answer.

lastStatus.description: The receiver's last HTTP status; null when it couldn't be reached.

callback.description: How delivery to callbackUrl went; null without one.

default.description: An option id (an array of ids when multiple). A single choice without one starts on its first option.

multiple.description: Let the person pick several options (checkboxes).

id.description: What the answer reports, e.g. partial

unit.description: Shown next to the value, e.g. $ or %

resume.description: The resume you sent, as is (null without one).

info.description: Create Events, ask people for decisions (an Event with buttons or fields waits for an answer), and maintain Organization-scoped identities. Operations authenticate with an EmitKit API key (`emitkit_…`) sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>`. The same operations are available as MCP tools at `https://api.emitkit.com/mcp`.
info.title: EmitKit API

get.description: Who the credential is: its organization, the Project its events go to, and its scopes. Works with any valid credential; use it to check a key.

401.description: Authentication credentials are missing or invalid.

429.description: The authenticated principal exceeded its rate limit.

post.description: Creates an Event in a named Channel, creating the Channel when necessary. When notify is true (the default), Organization members who turned on notifications for the Channel receive a web push notification. Events are retained for 90 days. Add actions with an id (buttons) or fields to ask a person something: the event waits for an answer (data.answer), which you read with GET /v1/events/{id}.

parameters.description: A caller-generated command identifier, scoped to the API key and kept for 24 hours. Reusing it with the same request replays the first response; reusing it with a different request, or while the first request is still running, returns 409.

Deleted events and events in deleted channels are left out.

get.description: Reads an event back by id, with its fields, actions and answer. Poll this to learn whether an event that waits was answered: answer.status is pending, answered, expired or canceled; once answered, answer.action is the pressed button's id and answer.values holds the fields by id. Polling every few seconds is fine: the rate limit is 100 requests per minute per API key, in fixed 60-second windows.

post.description: Stops a pending event from waiting when the answer is no longer needed; the answer page then shows it as no longer needed. Canceling an already canceled event returns it again, so retries are safe.

delete.description: Erases the Organization's identity for a user, deleting its properties and aliases. Events already recorded are kept under their 90-day retention, but no longer show the user when they are read. Pass the canonical user_id; an alias is not accepted.
